doc: The colour doctrine as tokens (D4 Ink and Hatch, D5 Inked Grime on top). The world is a black-and-white baseline: ink, paper and the charcoal / wash greys. Accent inks appear rarely and only on their allowed uses and layers: blood (the one saturated red: violence only), cop blue (an ink navy at the charcoal's value; cop_blue_hi for badges and light bars), vermilion (danger cues, objectives, the pickups that matter, Rivet's hazard collar; no longer cops or cruisers: that is debt, accent_debt.json) and teal (the souls, the dead). look_d4 and look_d4_item print paper / wash / ink from these tokens (look_profiles.json tones); PaletteTokens.classify() uses the gates below, in this order: blood when r >= blood_r and max(g, b) / r < blood_gr (look_noir blood_mask), vermilion when r - max(g, b) >= verm_gate, teal when min(g, b) - r >= teal_gate, cop blue when b - max(r, g) >= blue_gate (0..1 channels). dev/selftest/accent_audit.gd counts accent pixels per render layer and per body kind against these.

tokens.doc: the cream paper: pavements, roofs, the sticker rim
the ink: lines, hatching, the darkest wash
steel and robots before the print (look_d4_item STEEL)
blood, the one saturated red (noir's protected deep arterial red, look_noir BLOOD): spurts, pools, drips, splats, wounds. Never a threat or UI colour.
blood in its own shadow: a pool's body, a dried splat (look_noir BLOOD_DARK). Classifies as blood.

the police ink: a desaturated navy at the charcoal's value (luma 0.28 vs ink_2 0.29), so the black-and-white read survives; uniforms and cruiser body accents. Replaces vermilion on cops (owner, 2026-11-03).
the brighter police blue, for small marks only: cap badge, light bar.
